THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Budget season dominated central Wisconsin government this week, with Wausau and Kronenwetter both adopting 2027 spending plans, while Marathon County grappled with a bond default crisis and a heated debate over license plate reader cameras.

  • The Wausau City Council passed its 2027 budget 7-4, setting a mill rate of $9.10 per $1,000 assessed value — a projected $71.52 increase for a $200,000 home.
  • Marathon County's Executive Committee called a special full board meeting for Nov. 17 after a $347,409 shortfall emerged from a Bugtussle bond default on a $25 million conduit bond.
  • The Kronenwetter Village Board unanimously adopted its 2027 budget with a 6.79% levy increase and an assessed tax rate of $4.25; water and sewer rates will hold steady.
  • Marathon County's board moved $6,300 in Flock license plate reader funding to contingency pending a privacy policy review, following a contentious public safety committee hearing and near-capacity budget meeting.
  • Wausau's Joint Finance and Human Resources Committee approved a sole-source $214,521 purchase of Zoll cardiac monitors and ventilators for the fire department, passing 4-1 after debate over funding.
  • Wausau's Board of Public Works awarded a $967,994 contract to PGA, Inc. for the Business Campus Trail East-West Connector, part of more than $1.6 million in project approvals.

Coming up: Marathon County's special full board meeting Tuesday at 6 p.m. is the week's most consequential gathering, with the Bugtussle bond default and Hub City Wind Farm agreement both on the table. Wausau's Plan Commission meets Tuesday at 5 p.m., and the Kronenwetter Plan Commission is set to take up a septic tank ordinance amendment and subdivision plat review Monday at 6 p.m.
